ns2:section.sectionText: Topics covered: Fundamental laser and optics principles; Spectroscopy of chemical energy conversion at high temperatures; Linear and non-linear spectroscopy measurement techniques; Advances in high speed single point and 2-D imaging techniques; Turbulent chemical energy conversion in advanced propulsion systems; Ignition and oxidation chemistry of alternative next generation fuels. Prerequisites: Physics 212 and Thermodynamics ME300 (or equivalent) Grading: There will be two quizzes and one midterm exam during the semester. There will also be one final project (design of advanced diagnostics technique).
